body: Thanks for the report @thisch This is a third or fourth recent issue about the same thing, the fact that `pylint` appends the current working directory to the path, resulting in local modules shadowing builtin ones. It's something we need to address as soon as possible.

Here is a simple unittest that reproduces the problem.

```py
import subprocess
import sys


def test_issue2952(tmpdir):
    p_warnings = tmpdir / 'warnings.py'
    p_logging = tmpdir / 'logging.py'

    p_logging.write("")
    p_warnings.write("import mymodule")

    with tmpdir.as_cwd():
        # works
        output = subprocess.check_output(
            'pylint logging.py'.split()).decode()
        assert 'Traceback' not in output

        # fails
        output = subprocess.check_output(
            [sys.executable] + '-m pylint logging.py'.split()).decode()
        assert 'Traceback' not in output
```

I'm not sure if this can be fixed in pylint. The problem seems to be that

``python -m module-name`` imports ``runpy``, which imports warnings if run in the ``pytest/src/_pytest`` directory:

```
(pylint_venv_py37) > $ cd ~/gitrepos/pytest/src/_pytest
(pylint_venv_py37) > $ python -c "import runpy"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/runpy.py", line 14, in <module>
    import importlib.machinery # importlib first so we can test #15386 via -m
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/importlib/__init__.py", line 58, in <module>
    import warnings
  File "/home/thomas/gitrepos/pytest/src/_pytest/warnings.py", line 5, in <module>
    import pytest
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/pytest.py", line 6, in <module>
    from _pytest.assertion import register_assert_rewrite
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/_pytest/assertion/__init__.py", line 6, in <module>
    from _pytest.assertion import rewrite
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/_pytest/assertion/rewrite.py", line 16, in <module>
    import atomicwrites
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/atomicwrites/__init__.py", line 5, in <module>
    import tempfile
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/tempfile.py", line 184, in <module>
    from random import Random as _Random
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/random.py", line 40, in <module>
    from warnings import warn as _warn
ImportError: cannot import name 'warn' from 'warnings' (/home/thomas/gitrepos/pytest/src/_pytest/warnings.py)
```

I've read that ``python -m module-name args`` seems to be the same as ``python path-to-module/__main__.py args``, but this is not true, because running pylint using the latter command works in the ``pytes/tsrc/_pytest`` dir. 

Unfortunately it does not even work if ``python -m pylint`` is run from a different directory:

```
(pylint_venv_py37) > $ cd /tmp
(pylint_venv_py37) > $ python -m pylint ~/gitrepos/pytest/src/_pytest/logging.py                                             
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/runpy.py", line 193, in _run_module_as_main
    "__main__", mod_spec)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/runpy.py", line 85, in _run_code
    exec(code, run_globals)
  File "/home/thomas/gitrepos/pylint/pylint/__main__.py", line 13, in <module>
    pylint.run_pylint()
  File "/home/thomas/gitrepos/pylint/pylint/__init__.py", line 17, in run_pylint
    from pylint.lint import Run
  File "/home/thomas/gitrepos/pylint/pylint/lint.py", line 73, in <module>
    import astroid
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/astroid/__init__.py", line 63, in <module>
    from astroid.nodes import *
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/astroid/nodes.py", line 23, in <module>

  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/astroid/node_classes.py", line 38, in <module>
    from astroid import bases
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/astroid/bases.py", line 33, in <module>
    MANAGER = manager.AstroidManager()
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/astroid/util.py", line 26, in <lambda>
    lambda: importlib.import_module("." + module_name, "astroid")
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/importlib/__init__.py", line 127, in import_module
    return _bootstrap._gcd_import(name[level:], package, level)
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/astroid/manager.py", line 24, in <module>
    from astroid.interpreter._import import spec
  File "/home/thomas/pylint_venv_py37/lib/python3.7/site-packages/astroid/interpreter/_import/spec.py", line 12, in <module>
    import imp
  File "/usr/lib/python3.7/imp.py", line 31, in <module>
    warnings.warn("the imp module is deprecated in favour of importlib; "
AttributeError: module 'warnings' has no attribute 'warn'
```
@PCManticore This problem could be fixed by not using "imp"  (which is deprecated BTW) in ``astroid/interpreter/_import/spec.py``. See https://github.com/PyCQA/astroid/issues/681

issue.title: Avoid importing files from the local directory when running pylint

repository.name: pylint
repository.description: It's not just a linter that annoys you!

issue.body:
## Description

---

**Do not add the current directory to `sys.path` any longer** (ac2c4986)

Adding the current directory to `sys.path` can also mean that we're
going to load modules having the same name as stdlib modules or
astroid modules, which can break pylint.
We were doing this since 4becf6f9e596b45401680c4947e2d92c953d5e08,
but there was indication on why we were doing that.

---

**Add test for checking that files are not imported from local directory** (c8dc18eb)

Close #959
Close #2952

---

**Replace individual member imports with `os` in utils file** (50621cd5)


---

**Move _get_python_path in utils to be accessible by that file as well** (04d69fee)


---

**Pass an additional search path to modutils.modpath_from_file and friends** (814774b9)


---

**Continue adding the current working directory to sys.path with `fix_import_path`** (f80dd97a)

This behaviour was previously removed in ac2c49867077cea9d0542560590999f2ebe00276
along with the removal of `''` to not force `pylint` load local files having the
same name as stdlib or pylint dependencies.

But we need the current working directory in sys.path in order to properly solve
relative imports.
For instance, given a package `pkg` and two modules, `pkg.A` and `pkg.B`,
pylint would not be able to import a relative import `from .B import X`
because it does not know where it can look for `.B` in the first place.
Having the current working directory in sys.path means that
`astroid.modutils.file_info_from_modpath` is still able to solve relative
imports.

At the same time, having the cwd in sys.path means that we might still load
files local to this directory during pylint's initialization.
The second part of this commit is to move `fix_import_path` before doing any
AST processing. As a side effect, this removes a nasty bug with multiple jobs
linting. Because the path was previously modified before spinning up new workers,
those new workers would have had the cwd in sys.path and as a result, they would
have been "able" to load local files from the directory, such as a malitious `astroid.py`.

---

**Add more tests for loading a malicious astroid file** (8f07bf2e)





## Type of Changes
<!-- Leave the corresponding lines for the applicable type of change: -->
|   | Type |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| ✓  | :bug: Bug fix  |

## Related Issue

Close #959
Close #2952
Close #2969
